subject: math
intro: Every item below describes data that answer a statistical question. Practice reporting the center (a typical value), the spread (how much the values vary), and the overall shape (symmetric, skewed, uniform, or with clusters, gaps, peaks, and outliers). Items 1 to 5 are Easy, 6 to 10 are Medium, and 11 to 15 are Hard.

items.prompt: A statistical question produced the number of hours of sleep for $7$ students: $5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 8$. Find the median to describe a typical value.

steps: There are $7$ values already listed in order from least to greatest.
The median is the middle value. With $7$ values, the middle is the $4$th value.
Count to the $4$th value: $5, 6, 6, \underline{7}, 7, 7, 8$.
The median is $7$ hours, so a typical value is $7$ hours.

items.prompt: The daily high temperatures for a week were $68, 70, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75$ degrees. Find the range to describe the spread.

steps: The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values.
The largest value is $75$ and the smallest is $68$.
The spread (range) is $7$ degrees.

items.prompt: On a dot plot of quiz scores, the dots pile up on the right near the high scores and trail off toward the left with a few low scores. Describe the overall shape.

steps: Shape is named by where the tail of the distribution points.
Here the data pile up on the right (high scores), and a tail of a few low values stretches to the left.
When the tail points toward the lower values, the distribution is skewed left.
The shape is skewed left.

items.prompt: Find the mean of the number of pets reported by $6$ families: $1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 7$. Use the mean to describe a typical value.

steps: The mean is the sum of the values divided by how many values there are.
Add the values: $1 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 7 = 18$.
There are $6$ families, so divide: $\frac{18}{6} = 3$.
The mean is $3$ pets, so a typical value is about $3$ pets.

items.prompt: A dot plot of ages shows dots stacked evenly: exactly $3$ dots above each of the values $9, 10, 11, 12,$ and $13$, with no value taller than the others. Describe the overall shape.

steps: Look at how the heights of the stacks compare across the values.
Every value from $9$ to $13$ has the same height ($3$ dots each).
When all the stacks are about the same height, the distribution is uniform.
The shape is uniform.

items.prompt: A statistical question produced these test scores: $72, 75, 78, 80, 82, 85, 88, 90$. Report the center (median) and the spread (range) together.

steps: The $8$ values are already in order.
With $8$ values, the median is the average of the $4$th and $5$th values: $80$ and $82$.
Range $= \max - \min = 90 - 72 = 18$.
The center is a median of $81$ and the spread (range) is $18$.

items.prompt: A dot plot of the number of pets per family shows a tall stack at $0$ and $1$, then a gap, and a single dot at $9$. Name the features of this distribution (cluster, gap, and any outlier).
items.answer: A cluster (peak) at $0$ to $1$, a gap between $2$ and $8$, and an outlier at $9$

steps: A cluster (or peak) is where many data points stack up together: here the dots pile up at $0$ and $1$.
A gap is a stretch with no data: there are no dots from $2$ through $8$.
An outlier is a value far from the rest, separated by the gap: the single dot at $9$.
So the features are a cluster at $0$ to $1$, a gap from $2$ to $8$, and an outlier at $9$.

items.prompt: Find the mean of these $9$ daily step counts (in thousands): $4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 8, 8$. Write your answer as a fraction and as a decimal.

steps: There are $9$ values, so divide by $9$: $\frac{55}{9}$.
As a decimal, $\frac{55}{9} \approx 6.1$.
The mean is $\frac{55}{9} \approx 6.1$ thousand steps.

items.prompt: A dot plot of plant heights shows most dots clustered between $4$ and $6$ cm, with a single dot far to the right at $14$ cm. When asked for a typical height, should you use the mean or the median? Explain in one sentence.
items.answer: The median, because the outlier at $14$ pulls the mean upward away from the cluster

steps: Most of the data cluster between $4$ and $6$ cm, but there is one far-away value at $14$ cm.
An outlier like $14$ pulls the mean toward itself, making the mean larger than a typical value.
The median is barely affected by one extreme value, so it stays near the cluster.
Therefore the median is the better measure of a typical height here.

items.prompt: A histogram of ages has these bar heights: ages $6$ to $8$ has $5$ people, ages $8$ to $10$ has $4$ people, ages $10$ to $12$ has $2$ people, and ages $12$ to $14$ has $1$ person. Describe the shape and justify it by referring to the tail.
items.answer: Skewed right, because the tall bars are on the left (younger ages) and the bars get shorter toward the right, forming a tail toward the higher ages

steps: Read the bar heights from left to right: $5, 4, 2, 1$.
The tallest bars are on the left (the younger ages), and the heights decrease as the ages increase.
The short bars on the right form a tail that points toward the higher values.
A tail pointing toward the higher values means the distribution is skewed right.

items.prompt: A statistical question produced these minutes spent reading: $10, 12, 12, 13, 14, 14, 15, 40$. Describe the center, spread, and shape of the distribution all together.
items.answer: Center: median $\approx 13.5$ minutes (a more typical value than the mean of $16.25$); spread: range $= 30$ minutes; shape: skewed right with an outlier at $40$

steps: Order check: the $8$ values are already in order.

Center: the median is the average of the $4$th and $5$th values, $13$ and $14$, so median $= \frac{13 + 14}{2} = 13.5$. The mean is $\frac{10+12+12+13+14+14+15+40}{8} = \frac{130}{8} = 16.25$, which is pulled up by the large value, so the median ($13.5$) is the more typical value.
Spread: range $= 40 - 10 = 30$ minutes.
Shape: most values cluster from $10$ to $15$, and the single value $40$ sits far above with a gap, so the distribution is skewed right with an outlier at $40$.
Together: center about $13.5$ minutes (median), spread $30$ minutes, shape skewed right with an outlier at $40$.

items.prompt: Two data sets answer the same question. Set A: $\{2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4\}$. Set B: $\{1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 9\}$. Which set is skewed right, and how does the outlier in that set affect its mean compared with its median?
items.answer: Set B is skewed right; its outlier $9$ pulls the mean (about $2.7$) above the median ($2$)

steps: Set A is balanced around $3$ with no extreme value, so it is roughly symmetric.
Set B has values piling up at the low end ($1$s and $2$s) with a long tail reaching to $9$, so Set B is skewed right.
Find the center of Set B. The median is the middle ($4$th) of the $7$ ordered values: $1,1,1,\underline{2},2,3,9$, so median $= 2$.
Mean of Set B $= \frac{1+1+1+2+2+3+9}{7} = \frac{19}{7} \approx 2.7$.
The outlier $9$ pulls the mean up to about $2.7$, above the median of $2$, so the mean overstates a typical value while the median better represents the cluster.

items.prompt: A dot plot of shoe sizes has two separate tall stacks: a peak near size $6$ and another peak near size $10$, with very few dots in between near size $8$. Describe the shape, and explain why a single mean might not describe a typical value well.
items.answer: The distribution is bimodal (two peaks); a single mean lands near size $8$, between the peaks, where almost no data actually fall, so it does not represent a typical value

steps: Identify the peaks: there is one tall stack near size $6$ and another tall stack near size $10$.
A distribution with two distinct peaks is called bimodal.
The mean would balance the two groups and land around size $8$, the dip between the peaks.
But almost no data fall near size $8$, so that single mean does not describe a typical shoe size; the two peaks at $6$ and $10$ describe the data better.

items.prompt: A class records this data set of homework minutes: $20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27$. A new student who studied $80$ minutes is added. Explain how adding this value changes the spread (range) and the shape of the distribution.
items.answer: The range jumps from $7$ to $60$ minutes, and the shape changes from roughly symmetric to skewed right with $80$ as an outlier

steps: Original range: $\max - \min = 27 - 20 = 7$ minutes, and the $7$ values are fairly evenly spread, so the shape is roughly symmetric.
After adding $80$, the new maximum is $80$ and the minimum is still $20$.
New range $= 80 - 20 = 60$ minutes, so the spread increases sharply from $7$ to $60$.
The value $80$ sits far above the cluster of $20$ to $27$ with a large gap, so it is an outlier and the shape becomes skewed right.

items.prompt: A student says, 'This data set, $\{3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 12\}$, is symmetric, and the typical value is the mean, $5$.' Explain what is wrong with both claims and give a better description of the center and shape.
items.answer: The set is not symmetric; it is skewed right because of the outlier $12$. The mean ($5$) is inflated by that outlier, so the median ($4$) is the better typical value

steps: Check the shape: the values $3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5$ cluster at the low end, and $12$ sits far above with a gap, forming a tail to the right, so the distribution is skewed right, not symmetric.
Check the mean: $\frac{3+3+4+4+4+5+12}{7} = \frac{35}{7} = 5$. The student computed the mean correctly, but the outlier $12$ pulls it above the cluster.
Find the median: the middle ($4$th) of the $7$ ordered values is $4$, which sits right inside the cluster.
Better description: the distribution is skewed right with an outlier at $12$, and the median $4$ is the better typical value because the outlier inflates the mean to $5$.
